host: Modal x86 container (cpu=8 reserved, 32 GiB; Linux; AVX2 yes, AVX-512F no; rayon saw 24 threads; shared hardware, no load gate)
protocol: public-bench ann-qgraph on glove-100-angular 1,183,514 train vectors, --holdout 2000 (train only), vertex index: 4-bit traversal, 8-bit residual, degree 32, build ef 200, aligned rows, BFS reorder, 3-byte ids, rerank 64; arms A baseline commit a46108c, B tip df7df97, C tip with --quantized-search; round 1 cold build, round 2 graph from cache; 5 timed repeats per row; QPS = median over both rounds at the row selected by the fewest exact evaluations per query reaching the recall threshold
caveats: shared cloud hardware: per-round QPS medians differ by up to 2x for the same binary (B at 0.95: 552 then 1030), so the QPS ratios carry that spread; build seconds and RSS come from one cold run per arm; the container is not the GCE C4 host of the accepted rows and its numbers are not comparable to 877 QPS / 1435 s / 4317 MiB, only to each other
finding: On x86 the AVX2 kernels raise single-thread QPS at recall 0.95 from 426 to 799 (1.88x, per-round ratios 1.29 and 2.42) and the quantized construction search cuts the glove build from 249.6 s to 106.5 s (2.34x) and its peak RSS from 4310 to 1950 MiB (0.45x) at equal recall. This confirms on x86 the same-host build lever measured on the M4 and the kernel fix measured on linux-host.
